reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the refunds table against the refunds Alpha reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 231, 234, 235 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the order list to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders list shows three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
Refunds table matches Alpha's report, and acme's net balance is 36083. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme and birch have their net balances. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders list, so I'll fetch its net balance next.

All three net balances match my own check against the orders and the verified refunds: acme 36083 (no refunds), birch 10785 (32699 minus 21914), cobalt 29267 (30927 minus 1660). Nothing looks wrong, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 36083 is recorded. I checked birch's net against the orders and refunds: 32699 minus 21914 is 10785, which matches. Recording birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance is 29267, which matches my check: orders 232 and 235 total 30927, minus the verified refund of 1660 on order 235. Recording cobalt's payout now, the last of the three.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each amount matches the order totals minus the verified refunds: acme 36083, birch 10785, cobalt 29267.
